title: When to Use ‘Some’ and Not ‘A’ or ‘An’ (2/3)
titleZh: 什麼時候該用 some 而不是 a 或 an (2/3)
summaryZh: 說明不可數名詞為什麼要搭配 some，並用實際例句示範用法。
source: VOA Learning English (public domain) — Everyday Grammar

sentences.text: Some businesses have closed on my street.
sentences.zh: 我這條街上有些店家已經收起來了。

sentences.text: I gave her some apples to take to her mother.
sentences.zh: 我給了她一些蘋果，讓她帶回去給媽媽。

sentences.text: Now, let us turn to the question of non-count nouns.
sentences.zh: 現在我們來談談不可數名詞的問題。

sentences.text: Can we use a or an, or must we use some?
sentences.zh: 我們可以用 a 或 an 嗎？還是一定要用 some？

sentences.text: There is some bad weather coming.
The children asked for some money to buy books.
sentences.zh: 孩子們開口要一些錢去買書。

sentences.text: We would not say a weather or a money.
sentences.zh: 我們不會說 a weather 或 a money。

sentences.text: The word some is an adjective, meaning an unspecified amount, so it goes well with non-count nouns.
sentences.zh: some 這個字是形容詞，意思是不特定的數量，所以很適合搭配不可數名詞。

sentences.text: Of course, you need not use an adjective or an article with plural nouns.
sentences.zh: 當然，複數名詞前面不一定要加形容詞或冠詞。

sentences.text: It is interesting to compare the count and non-count nouns for related ideas, like letter, a count noun, and mail, a non-count noun.
sentences.zh: 把意思相關的可數與不可數名詞拿來比較很有意思，例如 letter 是可數名詞，mail 則是不可數名詞。

sentences.text: Sandy found a letter from her sister when she pulled some mail out of the box.
sentences.zh: Sandy 從信箱裡拿出一些信件時，發現一封她姐姐寄來的信。

sentences.text: Another pair of such related words is cloud, a count noun, and weather, a non-count noun.
sentences.zh: 另一組這樣相關的字是 cloud，可數名詞，還有 weather，不可數名詞。

sentences.text: There is not a cloud in the sky, so we should have some dry weather for the party.
sentences.zh: 天上一朵雲都沒有，所以派對那天應該會是乾爽的好天氣。
